deep.reconstruction:
Notation. Euler writes ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) for the double series Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y≤z} y^{-n}. The inner sum includes the diagonal y = z, so this is the non-strict double zeta value ζ*(m,n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n). ∫1/z^k means ζ(k), and ∫(1/z^k)(1/y) means Σ_k H_k/k^{m}.

The page continues §21, where Euler lists the 'linear' sums S(m) = Σ H_k/k^m that are always completely determined in every order λ = m+n, namely those with m = λ−1.

(1) Closing remark on the λ even case. The formulas on the previous page for λ even (for example S(3) = 3/2·ζ(2)² − 5/2·ζ(4)) are tied to parity. In them Euler has already used ζ(4) = (2/5)ζ(2)² and similar identities, so in his words they cannot be 'interpolated' to odd λ.

(2) Odd λ table:
- S(2) = 2ζ(3)
- S(4) = 3ζ(5) − ζ(2)ζ(3)
- S(6) = 4ζ(7) − ζ(2)ζ(5) − ζ(3)ζ(4)
- S(8) = 5ζ(9) − ζ(2)ζ(7) − ζ(3)ζ(6) − ζ(4)ζ(5)
- S(10) = 6ζ(11) − ζ(2)ζ(9) − ζ(3)ζ(8) − ζ(4)ζ(7) − ζ(5)ζ(6)

Euler remarks that nothing prevents carrying these over to even λ.

(3) §22: the 'properly interpolated' form, valid for all λ:
2S(λ−1) = (λ+1)ζ(λ) − Σ_{j=2}^{λ−2} ζ(j)ζ(λ−j).
He tabulates it for λ = 3,…,10. The general statement appears on the next page.

(4) Purpose (next page, §23). Equating this interpolated form with the parity-specific even-λ formulas yields the quadratic recurrence among even zeta values, e.g. 5ζ(4) = 2ζ(2)² and 7ζ(6) = 4ζ(2)ζ(4). That recurrence is the Bernoulli-number convolution Euler had proved earlier. Euler uses this agreement as evidence that the interpolation is legitimate.

This is Euler's celebrated closed form for the linear Euler sums Σ H_k/k^m, the cornerstone of the theory of double zeta values.
errors: No mathematical errors. I checked every line against the modern formula 2Σ_k H_k/k^m = (m+2)ζ(m+1) − Σ_{j=1}^{m−2} ζ(j+1)ζ(m−j), and all lines on the page are correct.
Methodologically, the 'interpolation' from odd λ to even λ is heuristic. Euler supports it only by its consistency with the known even-zeta recurrence (§23), not by a proof at this point.

ideas.what: Closed form of the linear Euler sum Σ_k H_k/k^m in terms of single zeta values, for every m ≥ 2
ideas.modern_name: Euler's formula for linear Euler sums / reduction of the double zeta values ζ(m,1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Goldbach correspondence 1742; E477, 1775/76); later reproved by Nielsen, Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn, Flajolet–Salvy
ideas.where_published: E477 (Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 20, 1776), this section

ideas.what: Separate tabulation for odd weight λ, with the observation that the odd-λ form extends uniformly to all λ while the even-λ form is parity-bound
ideas.modern_name: Odd-weight reducibility of double zeta values vs. even-weight behaviour
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (observation); systematic odd-weight theorem by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and others

ideas.what: Using the interpolated formula together with the even-λ formulas to recover 5ζ(4)=2ζ(2)², 7ζ(6)=4ζ(2)ζ(4), …
ideas.modern_name: Convolution recurrence for ζ(2k) / Bernoulli numbers via double zeta relations
ideas.where_published: E477 §23; the recurrence itself appears in earlier Euler papers on ζ(2k)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the canonical source of Euler's formula for Σ H_k/k^m, which is widely cited in the multiple-zeta literature. The parity discussion is also known. Nothing here is uncredited.
